use_case_name: Respond to a Second-Chance Purchase Offer

claims.content: To offer to sell the item to the 2nd-place finisher at their last bid price and enable them to accept, pay for, or decline the offer within three days from the time the email is sent.

goal.raw_text: To offer to sell the item to the 2nd-place finisher at their last bid price and enable them to accept, pay for, or decline the offer within three days from the time the email is sent.

claims.content: Customer
The Customer is the 2nd-place finisher for the auction, and there is a second-place finisher to receive the 2nd-Chance email.
The original winner’s order was cancelled after non-payment within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, and the item was placed into a “hold” status.
The 2nd-place finisher’s bid is not below the item’s unit cost.

No matches are found between the 2nd-Chance recipient’s account data and the Winner’s account data on Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses.

The Customer has received the automated 2nd-Chance email offering to sell the item to the 2nd-place finisher at their last bid price, with three options: Credit Card Option, PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, and Decline Option.
The Customer is responding within 72 hours after the 2nd-Chance email is sent.

The Customer clicks one of the response options in the automated 2nd-Chance email: the "I accept, pay with my On File credit card" button, the "Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments" button, or the "No Thanks" button.

trigger.raw_text: The Customer clicks one of the response options in the automated 2nd-Chance email: the "I accept, pay with my On File credit card" button, the "Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments" button, or the "No Thanks" button.

claims.content: The Customer clicks the “I accept, pay with my On File credit card” button.
This action triggers an automated process to generate an order and ship the item.
No further action by the customer is needed.

At main flow step 1, if the Customer clicks the “Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments” button: the user will be given three days from the time the email is sent to accept the offer; clicking this button will generate the order and load the Sign-In page; after signing in, the user will be taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page where they can pay for the order.
At main flow step 1, if the Customer clicks the “No Thanks” button (Decline Option), this releases the item from a hold status back into auction available inventory.

At main flow step 1, if the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

Exception path 1: If the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction; the use case exits.
Exception path 2: If the 2nd-place finisher’s bid is below the item’s unit cost, the 2nd-Chance email will not be sent; the offer is not made and the use case exits.

Exception path 3: If matches are found between the 2nd-Chance recipient’s account data and the Winner’s account data on any of Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses, the 2nd-Chance email will not be sent; the offer is not made and the use case exits.

If the Customer accepted the offer using the “I accept, pay with my On File credit card” button, an automated process generates an order and ships the item, and no further action by the customer is needed.

If the Customer accepted the offer using the “Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments” button, the order is generated; clicking this button loads the Sign-In page, and after signing in the Customer is taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page where they can pay for the order.
If the Customer selected the “No Thanks” button (Decline Option), the item is released from a hold status back into auction available inventory.
